properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL, AND NOT LEGAL ADVICE. Anthony, 2026-09-23: if somebody forks the repo, their work should be owned by reflow2.

⚠️ THE HONEST ANSWER FIRST: as stated, this is probably not achievable. Copyright in new code belongs to whoever wrote it; a license can set CONDITIONS on using reflow2, but it generally cannot transfer ownership of someone else's independent work to the licensor. A clause that tried would be unusual, likely unenforceable in places, and would scare off nearly every user.

IDEAS THAT GET CLOSE, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) FORBID COMPETING OR COMMERCIAL DERIVATIVES — via the license chosen in the sibling question (PolyForm Shield, FSL, BSL, PolyForm Noncommercial). A fork then cannot be sold or used to compete, whoever owns its new code. This is what usually protects a business like flo2.io.
(b) REQUIRE A GRANT BACK — a license condition that modifications be licensed back to the owners (a "grant-back"), so the owners may use and relicense what forks build. Closer to his intent than ownership; rare in software licenses and needs careful drafting.
(c) COPYLEFT-STYLE SHARING (AGPL-like) — modifications must be published under the same terms, so improvements come back into view. Does not stop commercial use by itself and is incompatible with the anti-competition goal unless combined with a commercial exception.
(d) OWN WHAT YOU MERGE — for anything a fork sends back as a PR, the CLA from the ownership question makes it the owners' on acceptance. This fully covers the work that re-enters reflow2.
(e) TRADEMARK — register "reflow2" (and flo2) so a fork cannot trade on the name. Separate from copyright, often the strongest practical protection.
properties.name: OPEN — can the owners claim work other people build on a fork of reflow2, and if not, what gets close?
properties.no_relation_note: No prior graph node on forks or derivative ownership; linked to its sibling questions from the same session.
properties.rationale: Kept separate because it is the part of his ask most likely to need reshaping, and a fair record says so plainly rather than listing it as one option among equals.
